drafts: The first controller was too aggressive: high steering gain and reverse speed caused the trailer rear‑right corner to hit a rail after about 9 seconds, leaving the hitch at roughly –7°. Only about 8.6 m (≈21% of the course) were reversed before time ran out. note.text: First attempt stopped after touching the left rear corner early; the controller kept reversing with almost zero steering correction, leaving the vehicle pinned and wasting 5 seconds and most of the 364‑second budget. Priorities: monitor side rails, keep hitch angle small by steering towards any swing while reversing, and if the angle does not improve quickly, switch to forward to straighten before continuing. Tip: glance briefly to the side to spot approaching rails; the mower can turn wheels 45° per second, so small steering inputs are enough.

note.text: Repeated left‑rail contacts (5) and many gear changes (9) wasted time. The controller stayed in reverse, only modestly steering, so the trailer kept swinging left and pinning. Prioritise early detection of a left‑side pin, then switch to a brief forward pull to straighten before resuming reverse. Keep reverse speed low (≈0.6 m/s) and limit steering to ±20°. Use the rear camera and left mirror to watch the left rail continuously. Trigger forward mode when hitch exceeds ~0.5°.

note.text: The trailer hit the left rail early because the hitch swung left (~15°) and we kept reversing with straight wheels. We never corrected the angle nor used a forward pull to straighten, so the trailer stayed jackknifed and the leg timed out. Prioritise keeping the hitch near zero: when it exceeds ~10° steer toward that side while reversing, and if it keeps growing switch to a brief forward move to reset the angle before continuing. Turn the head left to watch the trailer rear and the left rail.
